test: For each material PO with no receipt, check whether the same job has another PO of the same material that was received, and compare pounds (ratio unreceived/received). Break down the unreceived share by vendor, material, year, and PO position within the job (first vs later). Check whether jobs whose only PO for a material is unreceived still shipped/completed. Compare total material pounds per job (received vs ordered) against similar jobs (same part / estimate). Confirm GL material ties to all PO amounts including unreceived.
support: Most unreceived POs sit on jobs with a received PO of the same material and similar pounds (duplicate/reorder), concentrated in some vendors or periods; jobs with unreceived POs show ordered pounds well above comparable jobs; GL material includes the unreceived amounts.
weaken: Most unreceived POs are the only PO for that material on the job and the job shipped anyway (receiving-entry gap); unreceived share is flat across vendors, materials and years (systematic recording practice); ordered pounds per job are no higher than comparable jobs.
expect: Moderately confident the hypothesis weakens: orientation shows 28-30% unreceived every year and 76,049 of 76,730 jobs having a received PO, which looks like a uniform recording pattern (e.g., second PO on a job never receipted) rather than a business event. I expect the flat share by year/vendor to point to a system artefact, with the GL including the unreceived amounts either way.
